## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `--json` takes the next argument as its path even when that argument is another flag. Because of this, the combination the PR description promises, a default JSON destination used alongside `--junit`, fails or writes to the wrong file.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `--json` option to `parse_args` that takes an optional path and defaults to `results.json`. It moves the `--junit` assignment before the index increment, adds a `write_reports` helper that writes each parsed report to its destination, and adds tests in `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Skip flag-like tokens when choosing the --json path — With `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]`, `--json` takes `"--junit"` as its path, and parsing then raises `unknown option: x.xml`. With `["--json", "--junit"]`, it returns `{"json": "--junit"}`. The check is only `i + 1 < len(args)`, which contradicts the comment at line 12: "JSON can use its default destination when no path is supplied." — Users who put `--json` before `--junit` get a confusing error, or `write_reports` silently writes JSON to a file named `--junit` and writes no JUnit report. — Fix: Apply the `args[i + 1].startswith("--")` check that `--junit` uses at line 7 to both conditions at lines 15 and 18, and extend `test_json_default_and_explicit_path` with `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]`.
